summary: Piscataquis County, ME: state log lookout built 1910; removed July 2009, after which Homeland Security built a radio complex with a new steel tower on the site.

facts.design: Log tower of twelve upright logs, 22 feet high in the 1910 report; a watchman's house on top by 1919
facts.status_note: Removed in July 2009; the Department of Homeland Security then built a radio complex with a new steel tower on the site

events.note: Built by the state; 22 feet high, of twelve upright logs
Report calls the station still in good condition
Chief warden reported repairs to the tower and to the watchman's camp
Presque Isle Star-Herald (April 18, 1929) reported plans to replace the wooden tower with a 24-foot steel tower; construction not confirmed in the sources read
Removed in July 2009; the Forest Lookouts history says it made way for a new communication complex
Homeland Security built a new radio complex on the site, with a shelter and a new steel tower
Press release from Senator Collins's office dated January 27, 2009, on a state and CBP agreement to upgrade the radio tower at Priestley Mountain and allow CBP to build a new tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1910 report gives 22 feet and the 1920 inventory gives 20 feet. The two figures come from different years, so the record's 6.1 m (20 ft) matches the 1920 figure and is not used in facts.
The 2009 chapter report says the tower had no cab and held state radio systems; the Forest Lookouts history says it made way for a communication complex. Both describe the same July 2009 removal.

notes_for_editor: No source after 2009 describes the site. The Senate release (January 27, 2009) spells the name Priestley; the record and Forest Lookouts use Priestly. The story says only that a 1929 steel tower was planned; the FFLA Facebook caption dated to 1929 could not be read, so it is not used. Access is not described, so no access level is given. The record height of 6.1 m matches the 1920 inventory.
